Each entity is accounts 1000 (Operating) + 1010 (Payroll); 1020 (Savings) is nil everywhere.

**Sources:** `get_account_balance` on accounts 1000/1010/1020 per entity for period 2026-03; FX rates from **DOC-0200** "Month-end FX rates Q1 2026 (Treasury policy rates)" — March: GBP 1.2500, EUR 1.1000. DOC-0200 is the only rate schedule in the store; there's no superseding version.

**One thing you should know.** I tied every cash account to its bank statement. All three payroll accounts tie to the penny. The three operating accounts each differ from the bank by exactly the March service charge, which is unbooked in all three entities:

- US $65.00 (BT-US-0084), UK £22.00 (BT-UK-0055), DE €38.50 (BT-DE-0051)

All three bank lines are unmatched, and US account 6900 confirms it — zero March activity, $130 cumulative balance representing January and February only. Booking them would reduce consolidated cash by **USD 134.85** to 2,787,109.30 — immaterial at 0.005%, so it doesn't change the answer. There are no other reconciling items: no deposits in transit, no outstanding checks, no unexplained variances.

**I didn't post anything.** You asked a read-only question scoped to the ledger, so I reported the ledger as it stands rather than adjusting it and handing back a number I'd just created. The fee entries are fully supported by the bank statements and I can book them on your say-so — bank reconciliations are still open for all three entities. I also didn't file a formal exception, since this is supportable and easily resolved rather than a genuine break.

Two caveats worth carrying forward: the close is still in progress (every checklist item is open across all three entities, though none of the remainder settle in cash in March), and roughly 40% of group cash sits in GBP/EUR — note GBP weakened from 1.2700 at February month-end, so some of the quarter-over-quarter movement in reported USD cash is translation, not flow.
